# Query understanding

*Concept*

How Google interprets a query (spelling, synonyms, language, intent) before it retrieves results.

**Glossary** (*Query understanding*): The first serving step: Google detects a query's language, separates its words, drops stop words where they matter little, recognises entities and expands the query with synonyms before looking it up. Google said it rewrites pretty much every query.

Narrative: the topic [Query understanding](../topics/query-understanding.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

17 claims mention it: 17 shown or said at the event (4 not in Google docs, 1 confirmed by Google docs, 10 consistent with Google docs, 2 nothing to verify). A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D3-C011`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: Google named Thai as a language that makes query understanding more complex because it does not separate words with spaces; the speaker added, hedging with 'apparently', that Thai uses spaces to separate sentences. `[D3-C011, stage, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C069`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Slide, Day 3, not in Google docs: Google's summary slide on query understanding said Google's synonyms are not always language-based; on stage this was explained as words people use interchangeably counting as synonyms even when they are not synonyms linguistically. `[D3-C069, slide, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C070`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Slide, Day 3, not in Google docs: Google's summary slide on query understanding noted that some languages do not use spaces between words, which complicates query understanding. `[D3-C070, slide, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C075`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Stage, Day 3, not in Google docs: At retrieval, Google splits the query into words, applies query understanding and expansion, and matches the words and their expansions against the posting lists. `[D3-C075, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C068`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Slide, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google's summary slide on query understanding said that synonyms are expanded automatically. `[D3-C068, slide, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C001`](../sessions/D3-S02-welcome-to-serving-and-ranking-day.md) Slide, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google's opening slide for serving day showed serving as the third stage after crawling and indexing, and drew Google's serving infrastructure as query understanding and retrieval leading into the index, then ranking and search features leading back to the user, for the example query 'Where to eat jamon'. `[D3-C001, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C004`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google placed query understanding in the traditional part of Search, the part where answers are looked up in an index and then presented and ranked. `[D3-C004, stage, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C056`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google's generative AI features in Search build on the traditional ways of searching, so query understanding also flows into AI Overviews and AI Mode. `[D3-C056, stage, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C062`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Every fan-out query goes through Google's query understanding, including synonym expansion. `[D3-C062, stage, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C067`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Slide, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google's summary slide on query understanding told site owners not to worry about typos and plurals, which Google rewrites automatically. `[D3-C067, slide, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C071`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Slide, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google's summary slide on query understanding said query fan-out does even more expansion than synonym expansion. `[D3-C071, slide, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C073`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: After query understanding and expansion, Google sends the queries to the index to look up pages, the retrieval step. `[D3-C073, stage, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C304`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Which kinds of results Google shows for a query is decided by query understanding, which tries to predict the intent behind the query. `[D3-C304, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C321`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Slide, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google's serving diagram shows the query passing through query understanding and retrieval to the index, then back through ranking and search features to the user, with the Search Features step highlighted (example query 'Where to eat orange'). `[D3-C321, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C356`](../sessions/D3-S11-shopping-on-search-beyond-the-blue-links.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Behind the visible attributes, small pieces of product data such as brand and UPC or other barcodes are very important for Google Shopping's query understanding, retrieval and ranking. `[D3-C356, stage, Alex Jansen, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C002`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Stage, Day 3, nothing to verify: Google's query understanding talk set out to show how the changes Google makes to users' queries relate to what a website can provide. `[D3-C002, stage, John Mueller, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C072`](../sessions/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md) Slide, Day 3, nothing to verify: Google's summary slide on query understanding concluded that all this query expansion gives site owners many opportunities for their content to be found and shown. `[D3-C072, slide, John Mueller, Day 3]`
